answer_text: As of December 31, 2024, 6.0 million premises were connected to Turkcell's fiber network, and it had an FTTH network in 28 cities.

Delivery Hero treats the pre-August 2021 Spanish model as a probable risk, with provisions recognized and bank guarantees provided, while the post-August 2021 model is treated as a possible (not probable) risk, disclosed only as a contingency of €440.0–770.0 million with no provision. Glovo decided to progressively move to an employment-based model in Spain (announced December 2024, effective 2025) to avoid further legal uncertainty, while still defending the self-employed status through all available instances in the ongoing proceedings.

- Pre-August 2021 model: provisions are reflected because the risk is more likely than not to materialize; during 2024 Glovo had to provide Spanish courts bank guarantees to secure payment of liabilities claimed by the authorities (evidence [4], [1], [3]).
- Post-August 2021 model: investigations initiated in 2023 led to preliminary reclassification decisions in January 2025, but no provision was recognized since reclassification by Spanish courts was assessed as not probable; instead a contingent liability of €440.0–770.0 million (social security contributions, late payment charges, fines, possible VAT claims) is disclosed (evidence [5], [2], [1]).
- Glovo's decision: management decided on December 2, 2024 to progressively move to an employment-based rider model in Spain effective 2025 to avoid further legal uncertainties; this did not affect 2024 segment performance (evidence [1], [6], [8]).
- Glovo will continue defending the self-employed status through all available instances and cooperating with the Spanish authorities (evidence [1]).

Zalando - end of 2022: EUR 304.3m committed to fulfilment centres
Zalando - end of 2024: 59.5m EUR committed to fulfilment centres

The commitment fell by 244.8m EUR (304.3m − 59.5m), from EUR 304.3m at the end of 2022 to 59.5m EUR at the end of 2024.
Approximately 850,000 riders delivered at least one order for Delivery Hero in 2024.

In 2024, Zalando evolved Zalando Plus from a paid membership to a free-to-join model with a points-based system rewarding purchases and engagement, unlocking four benefit levels; it was tested in Spain and expanded to France and Austria, with further rollout planned for 2025 [1][4][6]. The accounting policies note that the awards create a separate performance obligation providing a material right [2]. At year-end, the report mentions increased accruals for the reimbursement of Zalando Plus subscription fees to customers at the beginning of 2025, included in "others" within other current non-financial liabilities [3][9].

Turkcell - 2G licence extension (April 2023): EUR 120 million (plus EUR 21.6 million of value-added taxes); paid in installments — an initial payment of EUR 81.6 million (down payment plus VAT) paid in Turkish Lira at TRY 1.7 billion during 2023, approximately half of the remaining installments (EUR 31.1 million) paid in April 2024 at TRY 1.1 billion, with the remaining amount to be paid within a year.
Vodafone Turkey - 2G licence extension (900 MHz): €120 million for a six-year extension until 30 April 2029 (excluding 18% VAT); paid the extension fee in advance with a capital injection and signed the extension agreement effective as of 27 April 2023.

Both operators agreed to the same headline extension fee of EUR 120 million, but Turkcell paid in installments in Turkish Lira (with EUR 21.6 million VAT added), whereas Vodafone Turkey paid its fee in advance via a capital injection (VAT excluded).
